# Slow Brew, Deep Roots

## Scripture

“But blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in him. They will be like a tree planted by the water that sends out its roots by the stream.” — Jeremiah 17:7–8

## Reflection

Good coffee cannot be rushed. The beans are roasted slowly, the water heats gradually, and a proper pour-over rewards patience—a steady spiral of water, a gentle bloom, a few quiet minutes of waiting. Rush it and you get a thin, bitter cup. But give it time, and the flavor deepens, the aroma fills the room, and the warmth settles into your hands.

Jeremiah paints a similar picture of the life that trusts God. A tree by the stream doesn't panic when the heat comes; its roots have gone deep in seasons of quiet. That's the slow work of discipleship. Morning by morning we come to Scripture and prayer like water poured over grounds—unremarkable in the moment, but over time extracting something rich. Trust isn't built in a single dramatic brew; it steeps through ordinary faithfulness. The days when nothing seems to happen are often the days the roots are growing deepest.

So don't despise the slow mornings. Don't measure your walk by the flash of a quick fix. Let the Lord roast out what needs refining, let His Word bloom in you, and let your confidence sink down by the stream. The cup that satisfies is the one given time.

## Prayer

Father, teach us to wait on You like a slow pour—patient, attentive, unhurried. Deepen our roots by Your Word, and let our trust in You grow richer with each ordinary morning. In Jesus' name, amen.

## One-Line Application

Give God the first slow minutes of your morning, and let trust steep.
